# Sigil

> Sigil turns an integer (0-9999) into one recognizable Cistercian-style
> glyph: a single vertical stem plus a small set of toggled line segments,
> one quadrant per digit place. The number logic is ~150 lines with zero
> dependencies; output formats (SVG, ASCII, DXF, Canvas, font, audio, STL)
> are thin renderers over one segment list. One repo: the spec and the
> golden fixtures at the root, each language implementation beside them.

## Contract

- [SPEC.md](SPEC.md): the full specification — data model, digit→segment
  table, quadrant transforms, encoder algorithm, renderer contract.
- [fixtures/vectors.json](fixtures/vectors.json): the golden test vectors.
  An implementation is spec-compliant exactly when it reproduces these.
  Generated by `sigil-php/bin/vectors.php`; never hand-edited.
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): what to read, and what not to change, before
  writing an implementation.

## Implementations

- [sigil-php/](sigil-php): PHP, published as `laxit/sigil`. SVG, ASCII and
  DXF renderers. Working.
- `sigil-js/` (planned) — JS/TS; home of the Canvas renderer and a
  `<sigil-glyph value="1234">` web component.
- `sigil-py/` (planned) — Python, for server-side generation.
- `sigil-cli/` (planned) — single dependency-free binary, likely Go or Rust.

Each is self-contained with its own manifest, dependencies, tests and
AGENTS.md. Nothing is shared between them except fixtures/vectors.json.

## Key facts

- Range is 0-9999. `0` is valid and renders as the bare stem.
- Model/renderer separation is enforced: renderers use
  `Encoder.segmentsFor()` and `Encoder.stem()` only, never `SegmentModel`
  or `Quadrant`.
- Changing the digit→segment table is a breaking change for every language
  implementation simultaneously; regenerate the fixtures in the same commit.
- Implementations release independently (`php-v1.2.0`, `js-v0.3.1`);
  Packagist and friends are fed by read-only `git subtree split` mirrors.
